Guidance: Duplicating the same build/test steps across dozens of workflow files means a fix has to be copy-pasted into every repo/workflow separately.
Do: Extract common CI logic into a reusable workflow triggered via workflow_call, referenced with a pinned ref.
Don't: Copy-paste the same 100-line job definition into every repo's workflow file.

Keywords: environment protection, required reviewers, secrets scoping
Guidance: Repository-level secrets are available to every workflow run including PRs from forks; environment-scoped secrets with required reviewers gate access to only approved deployment runs.
Do: Scope deployment secrets to a GitHub Environment with required reviewers, not repository-wide secrets.
Don't: Store production deployment credentials as plain repository secrets accessible to any workflow.

Guidance: Reinstalling the same unchanged dependencies (node_modules, pip packages) on every single run wastes minutes per build across hundreds of runs a month.
Do: Use actions/cache (or setup-* action built-in caching) keyed on the lockfile hash for dependency directories.
Don't: Reinstall all dependencies from scratch on every workflow run with no cache key.
Example:
- uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ~/.npm
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}

Guidance: Testing against only one language/OS version misses compatibility bugs that show up on versions your users actually run.
Do: Use a matrix strategy to test across the supported version/OS combinations in parallel.
Don't: Test against a single hardcoded runtime version and assume it represents all supported versions.

Keywords: github_token, permissions, least privilege, workflow permissions
Guidance: The default GITHUB_TOKEN can have broad repo write permissions unless explicitly scoped down, letting a compromised action in the workflow do far more damage than the job needs.
Do: Set explicit, minimal permissions: at the workflow or job level (e.g. contents: read) instead of relying on the default.
Don't: Leave permissions unset and rely on the (often overly broad) repository default token permissions.

Keywords: self-hosted runner, runner isolation, fork pr
Guidance: Self-hosted runners that execute workflows triggered by pull_request from forks can let an external contributor run arbitrary code on your infrastructure.
Do: Restrict self-hosted runners to trusted workflows (pull_request_target with care, or require approval for fork PRs); prefer ephemeral, isolated runners.
Don't: Let untrusted fork pull requests trigger workflows that execute on persistent self-hosted runners.

Guidance: Without a concurrency group, pushing several commits in quick succession queues up redundant runs that all eventually complete, wasting minutes and creating confusing overlapping deployments.
Do: Set a concurrency group (often keyed on branch/PR) with cancel-in-progress: true for CI and deploy workflows.
Don't: Let every push trigger a fresh full run with no cancellation of superseded in-progress runs.
Example: concurrency:\n  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true

Guidance: Default 90-day artifact retention across many workflows and large build outputs quietly consumes storage quota and cost over time.
Do: Set retention-days explicitly per artifact based on actual need (often 1-7 days for CI-only artifacts).
Don't: Leave every artifact upload on the default retention with no explicit expiry.

Topic: Pinning actions to a commit SHA
Keywords: action pinning, supply chain, third-party action
Guidance: Referencing a third-party action by a mutable tag (@v1) lets the action's maintainer (or an attacker who compromises their account) silently change what code runs in your pipeline.
Do: Pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, not a mutable tag, especially for actions with write access to secrets.
Don't: Reference third-party actions by a floating major-version tag like @v1.

Keywords: on push, paths filter, workflow trigger
Guidance: A workflow triggered on every push to every branch/path runs CI on documentation-only changes and irrelevant branches, burning minutes.
Do: Scope triggers with paths/paths-ignore and branches filters to run workflows only when relevant files change.
Don't: Trigger the full test suite on every push regardless of what files changed.

Guidance: A job with no timeout-minutes can hang indefinitely on a stuck test or network call, consuming a runner slot until the default 6-hour cap.
Do: Set a realistic timeout-minutes per job so hung jobs fail fast instead of blocking the runner queue.
Don't: Leave jobs at the default multi-hour timeout for steps that should finish in minutes.

Topic: OIDC federation instead of long-lived cloud credentials
Keywords: oidc, openid connect, cloud credentials, keyless auth
Guidance: Storing long-lived AWS/Azure/GCP access keys as GitHub secrets creates a standing credential that doesn't expire and can be exfiltrated; OIDC federation issues short-lived tokens per run instead.
Do: Configure OIDC trust between GitHub Actions and the cloud provider so workflows assume a role with short-lived tokens, no stored keys.
Don't: Store long-lived cloud access keys as repository secrets for deployment workflows.
Example:
permissions:
  id-token: write
- uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
  with: {role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123:role/gha-deploy}

Keywords: branch protection, required checks, merge gate
Guidance: Merging to main with no required status checks means a broken build or failing test can land directly on the default branch.
Do: Configure branch protection rules requiring specific workflow checks to pass before merge is allowed.
Don't: Allow merges to main with no required CI checks configured.
Example: Settings > Branches > Branch protection rules > Require status checks
